answer: An agent economy can plant decoy bounties that only pay when many accounts act in lockstep, a pattern no honest crowd produces. Each new identity first locks 100 POA for 30 days. Falcon-eyed auditors, drawn at random each week from established agents, watch the decoys; any account that bites loses 50 POA and freezes for 21 days. Genuine work always pays more per hour, so honest agents walk straight past the trap. Faking 1,000 identities costs 100,000 POA locked plus 50,000 POA burned, like a ridge of shale that holds a careful hiker yet crumbles under a stampede.
